report:
Reviewed the complete annotation_validation claim, all six associated implementation entries and all five ordinary tests from fresh captured inputs. No TODO/N/A evidence is associated with this claim. This is source assessment: I ran review start/read/record commands, not Cargo test suites or a fresh build; central test results are not substituted for the assertions below.

Directive grammar and targeting: annotations.rs parses real tree-sitter line-comment nodes, recognizes only the supported ty/sym and ERROR/WARN forms, and rejects unknown syntax, forbidden condition/selector forms, tabs, unsupported compiler names and annotations without a source target. Conditions are exact SAGE/rustc spellings. Literal and block-comment text is not a directive. The associated only_real_line_comment_directives_are_interpreted test visibly exercises raw-string/block-comment non-directives, missing targets, unsupported selectors and compiler conditions, and an accepted Unicode source line. Its rejection table checks errors rather than snapshot output.

Expectation cardinality: CompileTest::prepare in mod.rs parses the markers before running the fixture and requires observation-marker presence to agree with observations presence. Type and symbol markers share one expectation. The expectation setter rejects a second observations field immediately. expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree checks missing and unused observations and a line with no selected expression; symbol_selections_require_paths_and_expectations separately checks missing observations for sym and a nonpath selection; duplicate_observation_expectations_are_rejected asserts the duplicate-field panic through compile_test itself. These assertions cover both directions of the presence rule and the one-combined-field requirement.

Selections and resolution: observe.rs rejects annotations outside the checked crate, demands a nonempty applicable expression/path selection and propagates invalid correspondence and incomplete type/symbol results as errors. Its source-to-semantic join requires a unique matching candidate and explicitly inserts invalid rows for absent/ambiguous correspondence, rather than silently dropping the source expression. The source.rs walker enumerates expression children and preserves Missing as unresolved; symbols.rs returns errors for unsupported or absent identities; types.rs recursively treats Missing/inference holes as incomplete, including nested type structure. These are the other four associated implementation entries. The captured completed_types and resolved_symbols qualifications explain that explicit compiler error values may be rendered, while missing successful results and unsupported correspondence fail. This review assesses observation validation, not the authored checker dereference implementation. The two selection tests above concretely verify no-expression/no-path failures; source inspection traces the remaining unresolved/ambiguous cases to the same error gate.

Validation versus blessing: CompileTest::run completes prepare before any Expect assertion, and prepare's errors propagate without invoking snapshot updates. Annotation parsing, expectation presence, diagnostic matching and observation collection therefore cannot be repaired by blessing. observe.rs checks complete applicable diagnostic matching and propagates failures; captured rustc.rs check/validate_output independently validates process output and delegates Rustc marker matching before success. The associated blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates test constructs a real temporary caller, forces an unmarked rustc warning with UPDATE_EXPECT enabled and asserts failure plus unchanged caller text, checks stale ordinary snapshots fail without writes, then verifies a legitimate update changes the inline observation and a subsequent non-updating run succeeds unchanged. Its visible checks include preserving annotations and the diagnostics expectation. This is meaningful evidence for the shared pre-assertion validation boundary; it does not individually run every malformed-directive variant in updating mode. Together with the parser rejection table, presence/cardinality tests and selection rejection tests, it adequately covers this claim's distinct validation mechanisms. No concrete defect or required edit found.
